The peculiarity of the hole gas is the presence of a Rashba spin-orbit interaction cubic in momentum, possibly coexisting with a linear term, which results in the presence of distinct topological phases with Chern numbers as high as four. We map out the topological phase diagram based on effective single-band models with and without spin, and use input parameters based on a self-consistent Schrödinger-Poisson calculation of a planar germanium hole gas. As a concrete model for inducing magnetization in the hole gas, we consider the exchange interaction coming from the presence of a dilute ensemble of manganese impurities. A topological phase with $C=3$ could be accessible experimentally in unstrained planar germanium.

candidates.title: Hydrodynamic and photoionization analysis of a Cosmic Dawn dwarf galaxy based on a JWST-inferred star formation history
candidates.abstract: We investigate the evolution of the emergent spectrum of the Cosmic Dawn dwarf galaxy 2779 using coupled hydrodynamics and photoionization modeling. Evolutionary sequences of spherically symmetric, multi-component models track the star-formation history -- derived from JWST data -- from $z \approx 29.5$ to $9.5$. BPASS stellar population synthesis is coupled with the evolution of the superwind bubble and the surrounding nebular environment. The emergent spectra include escaping stellar radiation, nebular lines and continuum, as well as X-ray emission from the hot superwind cavity. At early stages, the nebular shell suppresses the escape of Lyman-continuum (Lyc) photons, while allowing X-ray emission to emerge. Significant Lyc escape appears near $z \approx 20$, followed by a non-monotonic evolution of the escape fraction ($f_{\text{esc}}$) and the X-ray luminosity per unit star-formation rate ($L_X/\text{SFR}$). Including diffuse ionizing radiation from the nebula can result in an effective escape fraction $f_{\text{esc}} > 1$. The model sequences terminate at a stage of stagnation or the complete displacement of the outer nebular component into a shell. A comparison with JWST photometry indicates that the final model spectrum generally reproduces the shape of the observed spectral energy distribution, although the overall flux level is too high. An illustrative comparison with a previous model having a lower stellar mass indicates that accounting for the evolving contribution of the nebula can reduce the stellar mass required to match observations. However, a more precise determination of stellar mass requires a self-consistent refinement of the star formation history. These models serve as a basis for constructing representative grids of models, as well as for conducting careful checks on whether dwarf galaxies could have driven the reionization of the Universe on their own.

candidates.title: Deep, label-free, volumetric lifetime microscopy via low-noise, single pulse sampling
candidates.abstract: Fluorescence lifetime imaging (FLIM) provides label-free metabolic contrast, but conventional time-correlated single-photon counting requires thousands of excitation pulses per pixel to avoid pile-up distortion, limiting imaging speed and increasing motion artifacts and photodamage. Here, we develop single-pulse analog sampling that combines sub-photoelectron read noise with a jitter-immune, frequency-domain estimator for accurate lifetime measurement at low photon counts. Single low-flux traces achieve a photon economy of $F < 1.5$ at 100--150 detected photons, enabling accurate lifetime estimation from a single excitation pulse in label-free, volumetric samples. In in vivo zebrafish eyes, single-shot acquisition recovered the lifetime content of 20-pulse averaging at one-twentieth the exposure, resolving endogenous lipofuscin heterogeneity. In intact mouse kidney, scattering and reduced photon throughput impaired lifetime contrast; this was mitigated by lightweight denoisers that enabled label-free lifetime imaging to 200 micron depth at one pulse per pixel. These results establish single-shot FLIM as a route to deeper, faster, motion-tolerant, low-photodamage lifetime imaging.

candidates.title: The Eclipsing $δ$ Scuti Binary HIP 7666: Absolute Dimensions and Pulsation Properties
candidates.abstract: We present a comprehensive analysis of the pulsating eclipsing binary HIP 7666 (TIC 308953703), containing a $δ$ Sct-type component, based on 120-s TESS photometry and 63 newly acquired high-resolution echelle spectra. While previous orbital solutions were limited by sparse spectroscopic sampling, our extensive radial velocity (RV) measurements enable a robust determination of the system's physical parameters. The primary has an effective temperature of $T_{\rm eff,A}$ = 7376$\pm$72 K and a projected rotational velocity of $v_{\rm A}\sin i$ = 56.6$\pm$5.3 km s$^{-1}$. Joint modeling of the light and RV curves shows that HIP 7666 is a detached system in a circular orbit, with Roche-lobe filling factors of $f_{\rm A}$ = 57 \% and $f_{\rm B}$ = 44 \%. The masses and radii are determined to better than 2 \% precision: $M_{\rm A}$ = 1.822$\pm$0.029 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm A}$ = 2.154$\pm$0.017 $R_\odot$ for the primary, and $M_{\rm B}$ = 1.246$\pm$0.020 $M_\odot$, $R_{\rm B}$ = 1.170$\pm$0.015 $R_\odot$ for the secondary. The binary-based distance (316$\pm$8 pc) agrees well with the Gaia DR3 parallax-based distance (313$\pm$1 pc), validating the derived system parameters. Frequency analysis of the light-curve residuals reveals 15 significant signals, predominantly in the $δ$ Sct pulsation frequency range. PARSEC evolutionary tracks indicate an age of $\sim$0.9 Gyr and a supersolar metallicity ($Z=0.03$), with the primary on the main sequence and the secondary located close to the zero-age main sequence. Galactic kinematics place HIP 7666 in the thin disk.
candidates.comment: 22 pages, including 8 figures and 5 tables, accepted for publication in AJ

candidates.title: Detectability limits of Ce abundances in Gaia RVS
candidates.abstract: Gaia DR3 provides medium-resolution Radial Velocity Spectrograph (RVS) spectra for millions of stars, but the extent to which they contain recoverable cerium (Ce) information across stellar parameter space remains unclear. We assess Ce detectability in Gaia RVS spectra and the reliability of DR3 Ce abundances ahead of the larger DR4 catalogue. We compute synthetic spectra across a stellar-parameter grid representative of the Gaia RVS sample. We combine the Cayrel equivalent-width criterion and the Cramér-Rao bound to map Ce detectability as a function of stellar parameters and signal-to-noise (SNR). We also quantify continuum-placement errors and compare the predicted detectability boundary with the Gaia DR3 GSP-Spec catalogue. Ce is reliably detectable primarily in cool giants at [Fe/H] $\gtrsim$ 0.5 dex and with at least [Ce/Fe] $\gtrsim$ 0 at an average SNR of 50, and the detectability region expands toward higher gravities at increasing SNR. Continuum-placement errors of $\gtrsim$1% become a significant source of bias, and at $\gtrsim$2% they completely prevent Ce detection. The criterion we present identifies where RVS Ce abundances, including those from DR4, can be robustly exploited. Outside our detectability region, these abundances should be interpreted cautiously, whether derived by GSP-Spec or by supervised methods. Currently, depending on the assumed continuum-placement uncertainty, between $\sim$40% and $\sim$70% of the published DR3 Ce measurements fall within this region; however, the rest are not reliable. Our findings are particularly important for metal-poor stars, for which the Ce lines in the RVS range are simply not detectable.

candidates.title: Observations of stellar feedback: tracers, diagnostics, measurements, and physical interpretation
candidates.abstract: Stellar feedback is central to galaxy evolution, yet the coupling of radiation, stellar winds, and supernovae to the multi-phase interstellar medium remains uncertain. This review treats this as a problem of inference, framed around four qualitative axes of ignorance: observational diagnostics are indirect; stellar population synthesis models must be ground-truthed before being used to infer feedback quantities; recent high-redshift observations have opened a new regime that may require re-calibration; and stellar feedback and the affected environment are interdependent. We examine the inference chain, from observables to physical quantities and from those quantities to how energy and momentum are transferred to the surrounding medium, across the principal diagnostics of stellar feedback: ionised gas, mechanically-driven bubbles, giant molecular cloud lifetimes, galactic outflows, and Lyman-continuum escape. We ask how much observations reveal about the link between the feedback-driving massive stars and the feedback-driven interstellar medium. We further discuss how stellar population synthesis assumptions, environment (e.g., metallicity, dust content), and galaxy properties (e.g., stellar mass, gas content) affect feedback measurements, and how high-redshift observations are testing calibrations established in the nearby Universe. The emerging picture is that interpreting a feedback measurement requires explicit control of the inference chain and of its physical context; feedback should therefore be contextualised, i.e. interpreted in terms of mechanism, gas phase, environment, and spatial and temporal scale. Progress will depend on measuring feedback-related quantities across the full range of star-forming systems and, more importantly, on obtaining observations (real, and synthetic from post-processed simulations) that match the same tracer and spatial scale across the same systems.
candidates.comment: Invited review for the Universe special issue "The Lifecycle of Massive Stars" edited by Jacco van Loon

candidates.title: Multiple spontaneous otoacoustic emissions as a single standing wave unstable to modulation
candidates.abstract: Spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs) have been interpreted either as cochlear standing waves or as local oscillations of hair cells. Multiple SOAE lines test both views, because each view must explain how the lines coexist. In the standing-wave view, each line is a separate resonance. In the intermodulation view, some lines are distortion products of others. Both explanations assume several independent oscillations. Independent oscillations, however, compete through the saturating cochlear amplifier, and the dominant oscillation suppresses the others. The saturation has another role besides suppression. The saturation also induces an oscillation of the gain at twice the frequency of the oscillation. In lasers, this oscillation of the gain, called the \textit{pump}, creates sidebands. This paper examines whether a cochlear standing wave can pump the gain by itself. A two-dimensional cochlear model with a step in the gain produced a single standing wave. The pump destabilized a pair of lines near the neighboring resonances. The other lines were phase-locked intermodulation products of the main line and the pair. A group of equally spaced SOAEs can thus arise from one self-sustained oscillation. The spacing follows the resonances of the standing wave, and the two explanations can hold together.

candidates.title: Horizontal component of the ion drag force in a plasma sheath
candidates.abstract: The ion drag force is responsible for the underlying physics behind many important phenomena in complex (dusty) plasma, such as void formation, particle alignment in an ion flow, shadow-like attraction between the particles, dust clouds rotation in the presence of a magnetic field etc. In this paper, we investigate the ion drag force acting on particles levitating near the sheath edge of a capacitively coupled discharge in xenon. In particular, we calculate the radial (horizontal) component of the ion drag force directed parallel to the lower electrode above which the particles levitate. The calculation is based on the actual information about the ion flow, which is directly obtained using Laser Induced Fluorescence. The calculated horizontal component is comparable in magnitude to the vertical one, which pushes the particles toward the electrode surface, and is higher than previously expected. This unexpected finding must be taken into account in future research. The very possibility of the measurements we report opens the door for detailed studies of dusty plasma phenomena governed by ions and their flows.

candidates.title: Resonant Trapping of Neutrinophilic Dark Matter in Supernovae
candidates.abstract: Supernova cooling provides some of the strongest constraints on light particles beyond the Standard Model, including sub-GeV dark matter (DM). While sufficiently large couplings to the Standard Model sector can trap these particles inside the supernova or cause them to decay before escaping, there typically exists an intermediate range of couplings in which their efficient production and subsequent escape lead to excessive energy loss, resulting in stringent constraints on new light particles. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time that, for certain types of DM-neutrino interactions, resonantly enhanced $s$-channel scattering with neutrinos can efficiently trap DM inside the supernova and can fundamentally alter the conventional supernova cooling constraints. In particular, we show that for mediator masses comparable to the supernova core temperature, this resonant scattering can prevent a substantial fraction of the produced DM from freely escaping, thereby significantly weakening, or even evading, the usual supernova cooling constraints on such models.

candidates.title: Selective coupling and spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states under local perturbations
candidates.abstract: In this work we investigate the spectral evolution of topological domain-wall states in a one-dimensional structure described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model. We show that a local potential applied to the domain wall induces a selective coupling between a topological state and specific bulk states. Moreover, by increasing the gate potential, we observe that the domain wall state energies asymptotically reach a bulk band, whereas new domain wall states appear on the opposite side of the band. As a consequence, the domain-wall-state spectrum evolves through a sequence of localized states that remain separated from the bulk continuum. These effects are also reflected in transport calculations, where the conductance peaks follow the evolution of the energy spectrum. To experimentally verify these phenomena, we realize an RLC topo-electrical circuit and perform impedance spectroscopy measurements. We find that the impedance matches the local density of states, exhibiting resonances at frequencies associated with the bulk energies that selectively couple to the domain wall topological state.

candidates.title: Global saddle selection and exact absolute-instability boundaries for convection in porous media with throughflow
candidates.abstract: In the Darcy-Prats problem, horizontal throughflow leaves the temporal onset of convection unchanged but raises the heating required for a localized disturbance to grow at a fixed point. The saddle equations give five candidates, but only the saddles reached by deformation of the Fourier contour contribute to the growth. For $Ra>π^2$, $Pe>0$ we prove that the same off-axis pair contributes throughout the domain: no Stokes transition can change its contribution. Its growth gives a unique analytic absolute threshold, first reached by the lowest vertical mode. Rescaling transfers the selection to Forchheimer drag, transverse rolls of a power-law fluid, anisotropic permeability, an open upper boundary and a vertical magnetic field. A shift of the same growth function accounts for interphase heat exchange in a model of metallic foam. At prescribed throughflow the threshold increases strictly with either resistance coefficient. In particular, a vertical magnetic field raises the absolute threshold at fixed Péclet number. Tabulated thresholds check the reduction. Algebraic elimination gives the boundary polynomial, and frequency recovery selects its physical branch. At the Darcy level the selected saddles trace an arc of the elliptic curve 11a3, a degeneration of a genus-two family at nonzero shifted levels. Series inversion on this arc gives an integer weak-throughflow series and an all-order strong-throughflow expansion. Rational certificates establish the exact convergence radii of both series on the selected sheets.

candidates.title: Data-driven exploration of the strength-ductility synergy in refractory high-entropy alloys
candidates.abstract: Refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) have attracted increasing attention for their exceptional ability to retain strength at high temperatures. However, current research mainly concentrates on compositions close to equimolar alloys, leaving a large part of the composition space unexplored. Here, we develop a multiscale framework based on a data-driven dislocation genome method that constructs energy landscapes for edge dislocation motion across various compositions. The local configurational force derived from the energy landscape is incorporated into dislocation dynamics simulations, revealing a scaling law connecting macroscale strength and atomic-scale local resistance governed by fluctuations in the local configurational force. Based on this scaling law, a new solid-solution strengthening model for edge dislocation in BCC alloys is developed, followed by a data-driven exploration of refractory alloys considering both strength and ductility. The developed method and theory are adaptable, allowing for extension to other BCC alloy systems and guiding high-throughput alloy design.

candidates.title: Unified constitutive model of body-centered cubic metals informed by discrete dislocation dynamics
candidates.abstract: Predicting plastic flow in body-centered cubic metals across temperature and strain-rate regimes requires distinguishing structural resistance from kinetic contributions. Here, we develop a temperature dependent mobility law for screw dislocation, integrating thermal activation theory and relativistic effects. Through discrete dislocation dynamics simulations, uniaxial tension and compression simulations were conducted on configurations with different initial dislocation densities, elucidating the correlation between plastic strain rate and key parameters such as stress, temperature, and dislocation density. Subsequently, a unified constitutive model incorporating temperature and strain rate is derived based on microscopic mechanisms. The model naturally bridges microscopic mechanisms to continuum response, resolving the additivity dilemma by establishing explicit physical criteria for how structural resistances and competing kinetic mechanisms superimpose. Through rigorous bottom-up simulations, we quantitatively capture the crossover point where phonon drag overtakes thermal activation, providing a mechanism-based explanation of anomalous thermal hardening. This work enables physically consistent predictions of strength and creep behavior across broad temperature and strain-rate regimes, advancing beyond phenomenological descriptions toward transparent, mechanism-based alloy design.

candidates.title: Magic of Dicke states: density, cost and yield
candidates.abstract: Dicke states are an elementary family of many-body quantum states, consisting of equal superpositions of all configurations of $L$ qubits with $n$ excitations. We show that their magic, as measured by the stabilizer Rényi entropy (SRE), is extensive at every filling $f=n/L$ except half-filling, and we obtain the magic density analytically, together with the subleading terms. In the context of fault-tolerant quantum computation, we also investigate the yield of Dicke states, and find that they can produce on average an extensive number of CCZ states (or $T$ states with a catalyst) at any $0<f<1$. This yield is not self-averaging, but fluctuates from run to run by $O(L)$, as if it were set by a hidden phase shared by all qubits. At half-filling, the SRE grows only logarithmically, while the preparation cost, average yield and relative entropy of magic remain extensive, so that a small SRE does not necessarily signal a weak resource. These results can be understood by viewing the Dicke state as a fixed-magnetization projection of a product of tilted spins.

candidates.title: Machine-learning charge density for electronic materials and devices simulation
candidates.abstract: We present a machine-learning (ML) charge density model, DeltaChargeNet, integrated with the full-potential tight-binding muffin-tin orbital (FP-TB-MTO) method for electronic structure and quantum transport simulations of materials and devices. The ML model predicts electron density from atomic structures with low linear-scaling cost, while FP-TB-MTO provides an accurate tight-binding representation of the system Hamiltonian. To achieve high-fidelity ML density for complex devices with interfaces and disorder, we train an equivariant graph convolutional network to predict $Δρ$-the difference between DFT and atomic superposition densities-under a charge neutrality constraint required for inhomogeneous systems. A secondary ML residual charge model compensates for errors in the primary $Δρ$ model. The predicted density is then used within the full-relativistic FP-TB-MTO framework combined with the non-equilibrium Green's function method. We validate our method on bulk HgCdTe disordered alloys (including vacancy defects) and Au/HgCdTe/Au disordered devices. The maximum band energy error is below 10 meV for bulk HgCdTe. For devices, the charge neutrality constraint suppresses long-wavelength charge bias that would otherwise distort the electrostatic potential by 0.68-1.88 eV near the device center, while residual compensation corrects the remaining 0.16-0.46 eV potential mismatch, essential for reproducing the correct potential barrier profile. Together, these corrections reproduce the layer-resolved potential, including interface steps and bulk-like plateaus, within 0.1 eV of fully self-consistent DFT. Finally, we demonstrate quantum transport in a 11220-atom infrared detector. By combining first-principles accuracy with linear-scaling inference, DeltaChargeNet enables large-scale device simulations without the full DFT self-consistent field loop.

candidates.title: Calibrated Period-Luminosity Relations for Mira variables in the Large Magellanic Cloud in the Vera C. Rubin Observatory $zy$-band Photometric Systems
candidates.abstract: The Vera C. Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space Time (LSST) is expected to discover numerous Mira variables in nearby galaxies, enabling their application for the cosmic distance scale. Miras are excellent distance indicators at infrared wavelengths, and therefore their period-luminosity (PL) relations in reddest $zy$ photometric systems will be crucial in the LSST era. We present first empirical $zy$-band PL relation for 85 oxygen-rich (O-rich) Miras located in the Large Magellanic Cloud based on time-series observations collected using the Dark Energy Camera (DECam) at the Víctor M. Blanco 4-m Telescope. The DECam photometry was directly calibrated using the Rubin Observatory Data Preview 2 (DP2) data. The observed PL relations were found to exhibit a break around a period of $\sim 300$ days, and therefore we only derived and calibrated the PL relations for Miras with a period shorter than $300$ days. We also explored the Rubin LSST DP2 data for known Mira variables in three Local Group dwarf galaxies. The $zy$-band light curves of Miras in IC 1613 are too sparsely sampled, whereas the DP2 observations of NGC 6822 and the Sagittarius Dwarf Irregular Galaxy cover only a short temporal baseline. For an O-rich Mira in NGC 6822, we obtain a distance modulus $μ= 23.32\pm0.24$~mag in good agreement with the literature. Significantly improved temporal coverage is expected in the first official Rubin LSST data release that will enable a robust validation of the PL relation in these nearby systems.
candidates.comment: AJ accepted, 11 pages, 6 figures and 1 table

candidates.title: A mesh-free deep energy method for phase-field modeling of thermally driven brittle fracture
candidates.abstract: Phase-field simulation of thermally driven fracture requires resolving localized crack bands whose paths are unknown in advance and thermal boundary layers whose thickness evolves during the transient. Neural energy-based computations of thermal fracture have so far started from defects placed in advance. This paper proposes a mesh-free deep energy method based on multiresolution neural representations that predicts spontaneous crack nucleation, crack spacing, and selective crack propagation and arrest under transient thermal loading. Two networks, each with its own multiresolution encoding, represent the displacement and phase fields and the transient temperature, and the mechanical energy and the incremental functional of the backward Euler heat equation are estimated on integration points redrawn at every iteration. Restricting irreversibility to the crack set, carrying the optimizer state across load steps and decaying the learning rates within each step help prevent spurious damage accumulation. On two notched plates the initiation peak loads agree closely with an independent finite element reference. On a quenched glass strip under an analytical temperature field the crack path changes from straight to oscillatory and then to branched, with an oscillation threshold close to the linear stability prediction. Under a prescribed boundary temperature a quenched ceramic slab forms a crack array of the type observed in experiment, with a spacing close to that of a published benchmark. On the slab and a quenched annulus the arrays are denser than those of a finite element computation on the same material field. No crack paths, nucleation sites or crack-adapted meshes are prescribed.

candidates.title: A Unified Device-Level Physical Framework for DRAM Read Disturbance
candidates.abstract: Read disturbance in dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) depends on both local device interactions and the electrical conditions imposed by shared array circuitry. Here, we combine DIMM-level characterization results, device measurements, and TCAD simulations to interpret RowHammer, RowPress, and ColumnDisturb within a unified device-level physical framework. We relate charge evolution at the floating storage node to three key mechanisms: trap-assisted electron migration (EM), capacitive coupling (CC), and sense-amplifier-mediated disturb (SAMD). EM is local and trap-sensitive, while CC weakens with wordline separation. SAMD extends disturbance through shared column circuitry by modifying unselected-cell leakage under rail-level bitline biases, a contribution supported by the approximately ninefold higher OFF-state leakage measured relative to retention-like conditions for a high-voltage storage state. These distinct spatial ranges account for localized RowHammer and RowPress failures and remote ColumnDisturb populations with abrupt changes at subarray boundaries. We further interpret prolonged RowPress activation as a transition from an initial RowHammer-like transient to sustained leakage driven mainly by SAMD under held wordline and bitline biases. Within this device-level framework, trap effectiveness and storage-state-dependent leakage provide an interpretation of previously puzzling failure signatures, including the earlier onset of 0-to-1 RowHammer failures despite the predominance of 1-to-0 failures at high hammer counts. The same framework explains the observed RowPress and ColumnDisturb polarities and the duration-dependent reversal of neighboring- and passing-wordline effectiveness. These results provide a physical basis for developing compact DRAM reliability models across access patterns and array configurations.

candidates.title: Polarization of strongly lensed gravitational waves as a probe of the lens-induced orientations of electromagnetic counterparts
candidates.abstract: Strong gravitational lensing is a well-established phenomenon in electromagnetic (EM) observations, where the lensed images and arcs are resolved on the two-dimensional sky and constrain the mass distribution of the lens. Strongly lensed gravitational waves (GWs) are also expected to be detected routinely by next-generation detectors, but their multiple images are recorded only as one-dimensional time series without positions. Among them, lensed binary neutron star mergers can be accompanied by EM counterparts with resolvable structures, such as relativistic jets. In EM lensing, the lens-induced change in the apparent orientation of such a structure can be measured only relative to other images or statistically, because its intrinsic orientation is not directly observable. In this work, we show that the GW polarization, which the lens leaves unchanged, provides this missing reference, i.e., a compass, so that the orientation offset of each image can be measured in absolute terms. We place this orientation layer on the EM image plane together with image positions from the lensed host arcs and Fermat-potential heights from GW time delays and magnifications. Using a mock population of such mergers observable by the Einstein Telescope and Cosmic Explorer, we find that the predicted image positions and arrival times are calibrated once the detection selection is included. The lens-induced orientation offsets reach tens of degrees and are detectable in up to a third of the events, at viewing angles above about $40^\circ$ for quadrupole-dominated signals.

candidates.title: Quantum spin-wave statistics and dimensionality in thermally activated magnetic transitions
candidates.abstract: A quantum correction to the rate of thermally activated transition between magnetic states is formulated within harmonic transition state theory and the Kramers-Langer theory by employing quantum statistics for stable spin-wave excitations around the initial state and the transition state. Quantum spin-wave statistics modifies both parameters of the Arrhenius expression for the transition rate relative to their classical values: the zero-point fluctuations renormalize the energy barrier, while the Bose-Einstein occupation of the spin-wave modes modifies the pre-exponential factor. Comparison of the classical and quantum-statistical pre-exponential factors reveals a systematic error associated with the excessive weight assigned to high-frequency excitations by classical equipartition. This error accumulates over the spin-wave spectrum and becomes increasingly severe with increasing dimensionality of the system. The effect is demonstrated for coherent magnetization reversal, and transitions involving noncollinear magnetic textures, including collapse of a magnetic skyrmion and rupture of a skyrmion tube, where classical and quantum-statistical predictions for the transition rate can differ by many orders of magnitude in three-dimensional systems.

candidates.title: Linear monitoring-feedback Model for Linearized gravity
candidates.abstract: Whether gravity has quantum degrees of freedom is a question of fundamental importance. We formulate a linear monitoring-feedback framework for gravitational interactions that includes local classical-record models of semiclassical gravity and, when quantum resources are supplied in correlated ancilla inputs, can reproduce linearized quantum-gravity dynamics. Auxiliary systems monitor the positions of massive bodies, and their records are fed back through a chosen gravitational response kernel. At the level of linear input-output theory, this construction makes the deterministic response explicit while exposing the force noise and correlations associated with the auxiliary sector. We organize the allowed ancilla correlations into three regimes. In Regime-I, independent ancillas have unsqueezed, uncorrelated sensing and back-action quadratures. A single object then has a minimum classical-gravity noise (CGN), S_F^min = 2 hbar M Omega_SN^2, where Omega_SN is the Schrodinger-Newton frequency set by the microscopic mass distribution. In Regime-II, arbitrary local sensing--back-action correlations are allowed, but the ancillas associated with different objects remain independent. The single-object CGN is then unrestricted, while the joint force-noise matrix obeys a determinant bound that is equivalent to the local classical-channel/no-entanglement bound. In Regime-III, cross-object correlations and a common nonlocal mediator are allowed. The commuting force noises can then be jointly squeezed, entanglement between the masses can occur, and--with a suitable retarded response and input state--the monitoring-feedback system can reproduce the noise and commutators of linearized quantum gravity, including non-Markovian quantum fluctuations.

candidates.title: Entanglement-to-Stress Relation from an Effective Holographic Description of the Transverse-Field Ising Model
candidates.abstract: We investigate an effective holographic description of the transverse-field Ising model (TFIM). We reconstruct the spatial metric from its entanglement entropy and determine the temporal metric using the Einstein-scalar equations, ultraviolet time normalization, and a smooth, horizonless center. Holographic renormalization then gives an enthalpy density that can be expressed through the entropy curvature at half the system size. This relation is a prediction of the effective gravity for the microscopic theory. We test it against the exact finite-size TFIM stress, which is not used in the reconstruction. Away from criticality, the gravity prediction agrees closely with the exact stress in the near-critical scaling regime. This result suggests an entanglement-to-stress relation in the massive Ising field theory, whose field-theoretic derivation remains open. We also find that the reconstructions for different system sizes and couplings share a common scalar potential, up to finite-size deviations near the center that move away as the size increases. This supports the view that the reconstructed geometries are solutions of a single effective Einstein-scalar theory.

candidates.title: Stress peaks and rupture in star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths
candidates.abstract: The tensile response of phantom star-polymer networks with bidisperse arm lengths is examined by energy-minimization simulations. Short and long precursors form short-short, short-long, and long-long strands within one end-linked network. The contrast among these strands, composition, functionality, and reaction conversion are varied, and their effects on network rupture are examined. At a large length contrast, two stress peaks appear over part of the composition range. In such realizations, short-short strands carry most of the stress at the first peak, while short-long strands carry most of it after the intervening stress drop. Interesting findings are i) that the peak stretches, including those in double-peak cases, follow composition-dependent master curves when plotted against cycle-rank density, as in monodisperse networks, and ii) that a recently proposed mechanical model describes their cycle-rank dependence, with parameters that vary with composition and arm-length contrast. The parameters differ between the peak series, although their separate determination is limited in some conditions. In addition, the Mark-type improvement of the mechanical properties of the networks by adding a fraction of short strands is discussed. With the implemented FENE force law, the work up to the global stress peak is closer to the long-only value, but an improvement above that reference is not statistically resolved.

candidates.title: DART ejecta reveal the recoil momentum budget of a kinetic impact
candidates.abstract: Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) demonstrated that ejecta recoil enhances asteroid deflection, but the ejecta processes generating and distributing this recoil remained unclear. We reconstruct three-dimensional ejecta evolution from time-resolved morphology and brightness observations, recovering previously missing constraints on momentum transfer and material transport. Integrating reconstructed momentum yields momentum enhancement factors $β_\mathrm{D}=2.13 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for Dimorphos and $β_\mathrm{sys}=2.04 \pm 0.19 (1σ)$ for the Didymos system. Combined with the measured deflection, the reconstructed recoil constrains Dimorphos's bulk density to $1435.18_{-153.71}^{+112.59} \mathrm{kg m^{-3}}$ without assuming its mass. By linking observed orbital deflection to the released material, this reconstruction provides ejecta-based constraints for assessing kinetic-impact effectiveness and investigating how natural collisions drive mass loss and debris transport among small Solar System bodies.

candidates.title: $^8$B Solar Neutrino Measurements of Solar Core Size and Temperature from 5805 Days of Super-Kamiokande
candidates.abstract: The detection of solar neutrino provides direct evidence for on-going fusion in the core of the Sun and serve as a probe for that solar core. Production rate of $^8$B is sensitive to the solar core temperature. Adiabatic flavor conversion of $^8$B solar neutrinos depends on the local solar electron density. Combined with the roughly exponential decrease in solar electron density with increasing distance from the center of the solar sphere, the solar core size, density, and temperature are inferred. This article presents an outer bound on solar core size and measurements of the density and temperature in the solar core based on Super-Kamiokande phase I-IV solar neutrino data. An outer bound is set for the solar core at $90\%$ confidence level as $0.499R_\odot$ for the high metallicity B16+GS98 Standard Solar Model and $0.381R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12 which includes protosolar accretion. A combined fit with the SNO polynomial coefficients improves the limit to $0.268R_\odot$ for B16+GS98 and $0.215R_\odot$ for K2-A09-MZvar-12. Results for other metallicity cases are also reported. In the high metallicity scenario assuming nominal solar core density and solar core size, temperature at the solar center is reported at $T_\text{C}=(15.599\pm0.0016)\times10^6$ K and $T_{\text{npz}}=(15.492\pm0.0017)\times10^6$ K at the peak radius of the $^8$B production profile.

candidates.title: Foundation Tensor Networks Generalize Across Quantum Lattice Systems
candidates.abstract: Neural quantum states and tensor networks have emerged as leading techniques for simulating quantum many-body systems. However, disordered systems remain extremely challenging in both frameworks as they require computation of the ground state for every realization of the disorder. Recently, neural quantum states have been used to construct foundation models that generate the ground state directly from the Hamiltonian. Still, they are hindered by the need to perform extensive sampling to estimate observables. To address these difficulties, we introduce the foundation tensor network (FTN), which uses a neural network to generate the tensor network representation of the ground-state wavefunction from the Hamiltonian. To accelerate training, we develop a technique, called \texttt{GridBP}, based on iterated one-dimensional belief propagation that reduces the cost of computing the energy expectation value to just two tensor contractions. We use FTNs to calculate the critical parameters of the glass transition in the quantum Edwards-Anderson model via finite-size scaling analysis. To facilitate rapid averaging, we use a moment-generating function to evaluate the order parameter, lowering the cost to a single tensor contraction. We obtain high-fidelity estimates for the critical parameters by averaging over 500,000 disorder realizations.

candidates.title: Dynamical Gauss--Bonnet Sum Rules and Global Consistency in Five-Dimensional Braneworld Cosmology
authors: Paulo Michel Longo Tavares da Silva
candidates.abstract: We derive an exact dynamical consistency relation for a smooth, periodically compactified five-dimensional Einstein--Gauss--Bonnet cosmology sourced by a real, minimally coupled canonical scalar field. For a spatially flat Friedmann--Lemaitre--Robertson--Walker slicing and a generally time-dependent warp factor, a contraction of the bulk equations eliminates both the scalar potential and the bulk cosmological constant. A direct orthonormal-curvature reconstruction gives the independent diagonal and mixed field equations and verifies the contracted Gauss--Bonnet identity. The integrated relation separates an exact total derivative from the dynamically active Lovelock sector. Importantly, satisfying the integrated sum rule alone does not imply a solution of the complete system. We prove that, for positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling, a smooth periodic time-independent warp factor and a canonical scalar exclude all exact expanding power-law scale factors $a(t)\propto t^p$ with $p>0$. This strengthens the previously established de Sitter sign obstruction and removes an earlier interpretation of $p=1/2$ as an admissible sign-compatible physical branch. For time-dependent warping, we reformulate bouncing conditions using proper time and the physical scale factor on each constant-$y$ hypersurface. We compare the common $w=-1$ geometric member with the perturbative weighted construction of Dias, Hoff da Silva, and da Rocha. At the level of the unexpanded Ricci-trace rearrangement, the curvature-only tensor contribution differs from the full Lanczos contraction by a definite scalar-curvature term. This distinction, and the additional independent field equations, delimit the physical conclusions that may be drawn from a necessary integrated condition.

candidates.title: SN Progenitors of SNRs in OB Associations in the LMC. I. Assessment of Methodology Using N63A
candidates.abstract: Color--magnitude diagrams (CMDs) can constrain the progenitor masses of supernova remnants (SNRs), but mass estimates for massive stars are affected by limited temperature sensitivity, extinction, crowding, and nebular contamination. We use the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) SNR N63A and its OB association LH83 as a benchmark to evaluate CMD-based mass estimates. Among the tested diagnostics, the extinction-corrected MCPS $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD provides the most useful constraint on the massive-star population. The $V$ vs. $B-V$ CMD is less reliable, while the reddening-free $W$-$Q$ diagram does not improve individual mass estimates because of its larger photometric uncertainties. Gaia EDR3 recovers bright stars missing or saturated in MCPS but provides weaker separation among the hottest stars. For seven spectroscopically classified stars, the $B$ vs. $U-B$ CMD-based masses are lower than the HR-diagram masses inferred using the same MIST tracks by $8.0~M_\odot$ on average, with a scatter of $7.0~M_\odot$. Isochrone comparisons suggest that most of the massive stars in LH83 formed about 7-15 Myr ago, complicating progenitor mass estimates based on the present-day mass function. Nevertheless, the masses of D243-1a and D243-2, stellar lifetimes predicted by the MIST models, and the empirical bubble-size-progenitor-mass relation suggest a progenitor mass of order 25-30 $M_\odot$. Our results highlight the potential and limitations of this approach for studying other LMC SNRs in OB associations.

candidates.title: On the Existence of a Third Planet and an Apsidal Resonance Chain in the Kepler-396 System through TESS Data
candidates.abstract: The possible existence of a third planet in the Kepler-396 system has been previously proposed. Given that the planetary mass is poorly constrained and the orbit could be either interior or exterior to planet Kepler-396 c, that proposal is not clearly known in the community. In order to address this and further investigate Kepler-396 system's configuration, new TESS data are employed to form a long baseline of transit timing. Using the pixel-level decorrelation technique, the mid-transit times are determined. Through long baseline transit-timing-variation technique, we perform a comprehensive exploration of the parameter space of the third planet. Two best-fit solutions, derived from different priors of orbital inclinations, have led to the reduced chi-square values as 2.24 and 2.34 respectively, compared to 12.97 for the two-planet model. This result strongly suggests the existence of the third planet, i.e. Kepler-396 d. Based on these two best-fit solutions, the masses of Kepler-396 b, c, d are updated to be around 9, 4, 4 Earth Mass, and the corresponding orbital periods are 43, 89, 144 days, respectively. With these updated masses, Kepler-396 b is on the border between rocky or volatile-rich, Kepler-396 c is confirmed to be a volatile-rich super-puff planet, and both planets lie in the Neptune savanna. Dynamical simulations with three planets are performed, showing that they are stable for a timescale of $10^6$ years. The examination on resonant angles leads to the conclusion that planets Kepler-396 b, c, d form a three-body apsidal resonance chain.

candidates.title: Crystal Structure Prediction from Search to Learning: A 30-Year Expedition
candidates.abstract: Crystal structure prediction (CSP) determines periodic atomic or molecular arrangements from chemical composition and physical conditions. Over three decades, CSP has evolved from chemical construction and global energy optimization to hybrid approaches combining symmetry, learned potentials, adaptive search, and deep generative models. This survey reviews method, software, review, and benchmark records from 1996 to October 2026, covering inorganic and molecular crystals, including formula-conditioned diffusion, flow, and autoregressive models that preserve composition. We classify methods by candidate construction and exploration: template and discrete construction, random search, evolutionary search, swarm and differential evolution, energy-landscape exploration, adaptive machine-learning-guided search, and learned generation. We distinguish representation, relaxation, ranking, and physical qualification. Benchmarks reveal no universally dominant approach. In a 46-target leaderboard snapshot, the best-performing template method achieves higher top-1 recovery than leading generative models, but paired tests show no statistically significant differences from several generative competitors. We also audit predictions for 68 experimentally examined materials, including 52 with structures confirmed by diffraction or microscopy. Predictions for 23 of the 68 preceded experiment, mostly through first-principles global search. Within the reviewed evidence, we find no independently confirmed discovery in which a deep generative model predicted the structure before experiment. We conclude with the principal limitations of current CSP algorithms and priorities for future research.

candidates.title: An Inverse-Designed Multilayer Selective Emitter for High-Efficiency Thermophotovoltaics
candidates.abstract: High thermophotovoltaic (TPV) conversion efficiencies have typically relied on photovoltaic cells that reflect sub-bandgap radiation back toward the emitter. Here, we numerically investigate an alternative approach in which spectral selectivity is engineered primarily on the emitter side. We optimize an emitter consisting of 16-layer aperiodic MgO/Si coating on tungsten, for coupling to a GaSb cell with an antireflection coating and an Au mirror. A detailed-balance framework incorporates polarization- and angle-resolved emissivity, multiple reflections, and Auger nonradiative recombination. At an emitter temperature of 1500 K, the optimized structure suppresses 97.1% of the incident-blackbody-equivalent sub-bandgap power at the source; a further 1.9% is returned to the emitter by the cell, leaving 1.0% absorbed parasitically in the cell. The resulting modeled radiative-to-electrical conversion efficiency reaches 47.0%, compared with 30.8% for a SiC emitter paired with the same cell, while maintaining a comparable maximum electrical power density. These findings indicate that emitter-side spectral engineering could substantially relax cell-side photon-recycling requirements and provide significant improvement in TPV conversion.

candidates.title: Predicting Individual Dark Matter Halo Concentrations from Their Assembly Histories
candidates.abstract: We present an empirical model for predicting concentration parameters of individual dark matter halos in cold and warm dark matter (WDM) cosmologies over z=0-5. Constructed using a large suite of cosmological N-body simulations, our model separately incorporates cosmic expansion (linear growth factor), mass scale (linear density fluctuations), halo mass assembly histories via the Extended Press-Schechter (EPS) scaled formation variable, plus a WDM damping term tied to the half-mode mass. It works for both virial and 200 $ρ_{crit}$ halo definitions. Across all tested cosmologies and redshifts, our global logarithmic fit gives concentration scatter ~0.09 dex for relaxed halos and ~0.09 to 0.10 dex for all halos. While relaxed halos maintain nearly constant scatter near 0.09 dex, the scatter of all halos at z>3 increases from 0.10 to 0.18 dex, revealing substantial violent-relaxation impacts on high-redshift halo structure. At fixed mass, concentration scatter is dominated by assembly history. We extract the scaled formation variable's probability distribution function (PDF) from merger trees and find departures from standard EPS theory. This PDF is narrower in WDM than LCDM due to suppressed small-scale perturbations and rapid, delayed monolithic collapse near the WDM truncation scale. Monte Carlo realizations with our formulae reproduce concentration distributions and match our prior peak-concentration model, whereas standard EPS underestimates concentrations from delayed-formation bias. Our framework offers a transparent, computationally lightweight tool to predict individual halo concentrations across diverse cosmological models.
candidates.comment: Submitted to ApJ, 15 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables. Comments and suggestions are welcome

candidates.title: Electric Fields Turn Vacancy-trapping Grain Boundaries into Li-Ion Pathways in Li2O
candidates.abstract: Ion transport in solids has conventionally been understood from equilibrium diffusion, yet ions in batteries are driven by electric fields. Does field-driven ion transport follow equilibrium behavior? We examined this question in bulk Li2O and at its grain boundaries (GBs) using electric-field molecular dynamics combining a machine learning interatomic potential with a Bader charge prediction model. Although Li diffusion in cubic Li2O is isotropic at zero field, an electric field renders it orientation dependent because Li hops along a limited set of crystallographic pathways that the field biases unequally. At GBs, this anisotropy becomes a qualitative difference: a GB that strongly traps Li vacancies but exhibits a strong field response releases them under a field, whereas a weakly responsive GB retains them despite weaker vacancy trapping. These results show that field-driven GB transport is governed not by static thermodynamics alone but by the angle between the electric field and the diffusion pathways of the constituent grains.

candidates.title: Pressure-driven evolution of crystal and molecular structures reshapes excited-state competition in coronene
candidates.abstract: Molecular nanocarbons exhibit unique optoelectronic properties and considered as promising candidates for organic device applications, however, understanding how molecular geometry and crystal packing jointly govern physical properties remains a fundamental challenge in π-conjugated molecular materials. Here, we demonstrate how these structural factors modulate the photoluminescence of coronene under high pressure. Combining high-pressure single-crystal X-ray diffraction, Raman spectroscopy, optical spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations, we establish a relationship between distinct structural changes and the evolution of competing emissive states. Our results reveal that crystal polymorphism modifies the balance between free-exciton (FE) and self-trapped-exciton (STE) emission, while pressure-induced molecular bending is associated with a nonmonotonic evolution of STE emission. As intermolecular distances shorten, enhanced intermolecular electronic interactions give rise to excimer-related emission, introducing an additional emissive pathway. Although pressure-dependent optical properties of coronene have been linked to changes in crystal packing, our findings highlight that the optical response of a molecular solid is not governed by molecular deformation or crystal packing alone, but emerges from their interplay with intermolecular electronic coupling. By directly resolving molecular bending alongside changes in excited-state emission, this work provides insight into how distinct structural degrees of freedom can reshape the photophysical behavior of π-conjugated molecular solids.

candidates.title: Spatial scaling of heterogeneity transfer from boron concentration to absorbed dose in boron neutron capture therapy
candidates.abstract: We investigate how the amplitude and spatial correlation length of boron-concentration fluctuations affect the boron-induced absorbed-dose distribution in boron neutron capture therapy (BNCT). The spatial energy-deposition response of alpha particles and lithium nuclei is obtained using Geant4 and convolved with three-dimensional correlated lognormal boron fields under a uniform neutron field. Approximately $90\%$ of the reaction-product energy is deposited within a radius of $6.00~μ\mathrm{m}$, with a characteristic deposition length of $\ell_B\approx2.05~μ\mathrm{m}$. Dose heterogeneity increases with both the fluctuation amplitude $H$ and correlation length $ξ$, while the transfer factor $S=CV_D/H$ exhibits an approximate scaling collapse as a function of $ξ/\ell_B$. Analytical Gaussian and lognormal--Gaussian models provide reference predictions for this behavior. At short correlation lengths, the Geant4 response yields a higher transfer factor than a Gaussian response with the same characteristic length, highlighting the influence of the energy-deposition shape on dose smoothing. For $D_{95}$, defined as the dose received by at least $95\%$ of the modeled volume, the relative difference between homogeneous and heterogeneous boron-dose models reaches $(86.62\pm1.07)\%$ at $H=1.2$ and a target ratio $ξ/\ell_B=6$. We show that mean boron concentration alone is insufficient to characterize spatial nonuniformity of the boron-dose component.

candidates.title: An AI-enabled high-resolution chlorophyll-a forecasting model that outperforms the operational global biogeochemical system
candidates.abstract: Surface chlorophyll-a concentration is a key indicator of marine phytoplankton variability, and short-term forecasts of its distribution provide advance information for marine ecosystem monitoring and management. However, interactions between physical transport and biological processes complicate chlorophyll-a forecasting, and simulating these coupled processes with conventional numerical models imposes substantial computational demands. Here we introduce ChlCast, an AI model that generates daily forecasts of surface chlorophyll-a concentration over a 10-day horizon at approximately 4-km resolution between 60$^\circ$S and 60$^\circ$N. ChlCast combines factorized spatiotemporal convolutions with a multiscale architecture to learn from historical chlorophyll-a fields and climatological information. Compared with the operational 0.25$^\circ$ Copernicus global ocean biogeochemical forecasting system, ChlCast reduces mean absolute error and root mean square error by 70.74% and 47.63%, respectively, against satellite-derived Level-4 chlorophyll-a fields, and by 35.03% and 13.07% against independent BGC-Argo in situ observations. Coastal case studies further show that the 4-km forecasts retain coastal gradients and localized concentration maxima that are weakened by coarse-grid averaging. These results demonstrate the potential of observation-driven deep learning for high-resolution forecasting of surface chlorophyll-a variability at the near-global scale.

candidates.title: Theoretical exploration of ambient-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate: A strategy of atomic substitution for tuning chemical pressure
candidates.abstract: The possibility of ambient-pressure superconductivity in $\mathrm{La_3Ni_2O_7}$ is theoretically explored via chemical substitution. Using first-principles and many-body calculations, we propose substituting $\mathrm{Ba}$ at the lanthanide site to exert chemical pressure, thereby mitigating the octahedral distortions that suppress superconductivity. Phonon calculations demonstrate the dynamical stability of the high-symmetry tetragonal phase in $\mathrm{La_{3-\it{x}}Ba_{\it{x}}Ni_2O_7}$ at a small doping ratio of $x \sim 0.15$. By applying the fluctuation exchange approximation to an effective model Hamiltonian derived from this stable structure, we calculate the Eliashberg eigenvalue $λ$ to evaluate the relative superconducting transition temperature $T_\mathrm{c}$ to existing unconventional superconductors. We conclude that $s_\pm$-wave superconductivity is likely to emerge, as the required $\mathrm{Ba}$ concentration ($x \sim 0.15$) is sufficiently small to minimize the detrimental suppression of superconductivity induced by hole doping.

candidates.title: Learning and Generating Time Trajectories of Multidimensional Stochastic Processes
candidates.abstract: We present a multidimensional statistics-informed neural network (SINN) framework for learning and generating trajectories of multicomponent stochastic processes. SINN is built upon a deterministic recurrent neural network that takes streams of white-noise sequences as input and generates ensembles of stochastic trajectories whose statistical properties match those of the underlying stochastic dynamics. While SINN has been demonstrated for various one-dimensional non-Markovian processes, extending it to multidimensional processes is essential for real-world applications. Here, we present key developments toward this goal. First, because direct estimation of multivariate probability density functions (PDFs) becomes computationally challenging with increasing dimension, we represent joint-distribution information using collections of one-dimensional PDFs constructed from linear combinations of the process components. Second, to accommodate the larger set of statistical objectives required to characterize multidimensional processes, we adopt a self-adaptive loss-balancing strategy that dynamically weights the components of the total loss function. Third, we introduce a reference-normalized validation framework that interprets statistical discrepancies relative to the finite-sample variability between independent target ensembles. We also investigate the role of the input white-noise dimension in SINN performance. We evaluate the proposed approach using a Langevin benchmark based on two coupled Duffing oscillators and further demonstrate its applicability to the Langevin dynamics of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam chain and kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of a lattice Lotka-Volterra model. Our results demonstrate that the multidimensional SINN framework provides a practical approach for modeling multidimensional stochastic dynamics.

candidates.title: Anyon Proliferation at Self-Triality: From a Lattice Model to Adjoint QCD$_3$
candidates.abstract: We study how competitive proliferation among three types of anyons in a self-trial $\mathbb{Z}_2\times\mathbb{Z}_2$ gauge theory can drive symmetry breaking while preserving part of the topological order. We construct a deformation of the honeycomb color code, a spin model rooted in quantum error correction, with an $S_3$ symmetry that permutes the competing anyons, together with time-reversal and fermionic $\mathbb{Z}_2^{(1)}$ one-form symmetries. We propose two dual continuum descriptions of this transition. The bosonic description is a $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_3\times\mathrm{Spin}(8)_{-1}$ Chern-Simons-Higgs theory with a real Higgs field in the $(\mathbf{8}_{\mathrm{adj}},\mathbf{8}_v)$ representation. Fermion-boson duality gives a particularly simple fermionic dual: $\mathrm{PSU}(3)_{3/2}$ QCD$_3$ with a single adjoint Majorana fermion and gauged fermion parity. Both descriptions match the lattice model's unitary symmetries and proposed phase diagram, connecting double-toric-code order to a symmetry-broken phase with residual toric-code order. The transition is described by Higgs condensation and by a Majorana mass changing sign, respectively. The continuum theories are proposed to recover lattice time reversal at criticality. This connection to adjoint QCD$_3$ points to a possible continuous $S_3$-breaking transition from competing anyons, in contrast to the conventional first-order three-state Potts transition from competing local order parameters.
candidates.comment: 14 pages, 1 figure, 1 table; includes Supplemental Material

candidates.title: Axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant: Bayesian constraints from current cosmological data
candidates.abstract: We constrain canonical axion quintessence with a negative cosmological constant using DES Year 5 supernovae, DESI DR2 BAO, compressed CMB information, and geometry-corrected Gold-2017 growth data. We solve the background and linear-growth equations and sample with PolyChord. Our joint prior is logarithmic in the decay constant over $0.005\leq f/M_{\rm Pl}\leq10$ and uniform in the initial angle $θ_i=φ_i/f\in[0,π]$, conditioned on $π-θ_i\geq H_{\rm inf}/(2πf)$ with $H_{\rm inf}=10^{13}$ GeV and reduced Planck mass $M_{\rm Pl}$. The broad-prior model favors recent thawing, with median $w_{{\rm DE},0}=-0.865^{+0.068}_{-0.053}$, $m_φ\in[0.91,4.39]\times10^{-33}$ eV, and $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.589,4.899]$ (central 68\% credible intervals). Bayes factors relative to flat $Λ$CDM are 0.70 and 30.1 for the normalized fluctuation-conditioned prior (Convention I) and its further conditioning on numerical acceptance (Convention II). Restricting $f\leq M_{\rm Pl}$ gives $f/M_{\rm Pl}\in[0.262,0.822]$ at 68\% credibility and Bayes factors 0.233 and 32.4. Relative to the zero-vacuum axion model, the broad-prior Bayes factors are 0.620 and 1.65, providing no compelling evidence for a negative cosmological constant. Local likelihood optimization gives an Akaike information criterion difference $Δ{\rm AIC}\simeq-10.87$ for the zero-vacuum model relative to flat $Λ$CDM. For this model, assuming that the instanton generating $m_φ^2f^2=Λ_{\rm UV}^4e^{-S_{\rm inst}}$ satisfies the axionic Weak Gravity Conjecture, the one-sided 95\% posterior lower limit on the minimum compatible coefficient $c_{\min}$ rises from 37 to 55 as the ultraviolet scale $Λ_{\rm UV}$ increases from $10^{-10}M_{\rm Pl}$ to $M_{\rm Pl}$, in tension with an order-one coefficient under these assumptions.

candidates.title: Dopant-vacancy complexes as single-photon-emitter candidates in monolayer silicon carbide: radiative and nonradiative decay
candidates.abstract: Solid-state color centers have emerged as promising single-photon sources (SPSs). In particular, color centers in two-dimensional (2D) materials combine high photon brightness with scalable fabrication and ease of integration, offering a versatile platform for quantum information technologies. Realizing high-efficiency SPSs, however, requires strong radiative emission and negligible nonradiative decay. Using first-principles calculations, we assess radiative and nonradiative decay in dopant-vacancy complexes XSiVC (X = N, O, P, and S) in monolayer silicon carbide. All four defects exhibit stable neutral charge states and inter-defect optical transitions. Among them, PSiVC emerges as the leading single-photon-emitter candidate, combining rapid radiative decay with negligible nonradiative decay and a near-unity quantum yield within the modeled channels. By contrast, multiphonon decay limits the quantum yield of NSiVC despite its high Debye-Waller factor. Hyperfine tensors provide characteristic signatures for identifying the spin-active centers. Beyond identifying promising candidates, these results establish a joint radiative-nonradiative screening strategy and provide theoretical guidance for the rational design of color centers as solid-state SPSs.

candidates.title: Ultrafast Imaging Reveals Energy Transport Anisotropy Grows from Bulk to Monolayer Black Phosphorus
candidates.abstract: Black phosphorus is an emerging low-dimensional semiconductor whose tunable band gap, high carrier mobility, and anisotropic transport make it attractive for directional energy transport in electronics and thermoelectrics. Using ultrafast stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy (stroboSCAT), we image spatiotemporal evolution of energy carriers with picosecond resolution, simultaneously resolving heat and charge transport in bulk black phosphorus and exciton transport in the monolayer. The in-plane armchair:zigzag anisotropy increases from 5.3:1 in the bulk to 6.7:1 in the monolayer, driven by enhanced armchair exciton diffusivity (45.5 cm$^2$/s) relative to bulk armchair charge carriers (16.5 cm$^2$/s). The monolayer anisotropy is smaller than the calculated exciton dispersion alone would suggest, which first-principles calculations attribute to preferential exciton-phonon scattering to large momenta along the zigzag direction. These directly measured, layer-resolved diffusivities identify armchair-aligned monolayers as the optimal geometry for directional transport and show that transport anisotropy cannot be inferred from band dispersion alone.

candidates.title: Counter-rotating Ionized and Neutral Gas in a Star-forming Elliptical Galaxy
candidates.abstract: In early-type galaxies, gas that is kinematically misaligned with the stars generally rotates together across all gas phases, implying a single external origin. Using upgraded Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (uGMRT) 21 cm imaging and SDSS-MaNGA spatially resolved spectroscopy, we studied MaNGA 10214-1902, a compact ($R_e = 0.78$ kpc), star-forming elliptical galaxy with stellar mass $\log M_*/M_{\odot} = 9.90$, in which the ionized gas counter-rotates with respect to the stars. It hosts $\log(M_{\rm HI}/M_{\odot}) = 9.65$ in a 45 kpc HI disk that co-rotates with the stars and has a central column-density depression. Inside this depression, the ionized gas ($r \lesssim 2$ kpc) rotates in the opposite sense to both the stars ($Δ{\rm PA} = 152^\circ \pm 20^\circ$) and the HI that surrounds it ($Δ{\rm PA} = 179^\circ \pm 10^\circ$). HI co-spatial with the ionized gas is not detected, so a fainter inner HI component with a different orientation cannot be ruled out. This central gas is star-forming in the [SII] and [OI] diagnostic diagrams and has EW(HI) $>6~\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ at the center. The 1.4 GHz radio-continuum star formation rate agrees with the spectral energy distribution based value, showing no evidence of a dominant active galactic nucleus. The stellar population at the center is younger than the outskirts and has the lowest D$_{\rm n}$4000. These results are consistent with the acquisition of gas with opposite angular momentum into the center of a pre-existing HI disk that co-rotates with the stars, which can fuel the most recent central star formation.
candidates.comment: 16 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to ApJL

candidates.title: A passive, battery-free flexible metasurface for implantable millimetre-wave radar glucose sensing
candidates.abstract: Continuous glucose monitors (CGM) break the skin barrier and require periodic sensor replacement. We investigated whether a passive, battery-free flexible metasurface, implanted beneath tissue and read by a commercial 60 GHz radar, can track blood glucose levels. The metasurface contained no electronics or reagents. We fitted a conical helix to the in-phase and quadrature radar signals across the frequency sweep and used its mean radius (the spiral radius) as the glucose-dependent feature. We tested glucose concentrations of 25 to 400 mg/dL in saline solution with and without the metasurface, and 196 to 596 mg/dL of total glucose in porcine whole blood beneath ex vivo porcine tissue and in a murine cadaver model with pulsatile blood flow. The metasurface was essential for achieving a monotonic sensor response; in saline, the coefficient of determination ($R^2$) of a logarithmic fit increased from 0.18 without the metasurface to 0.90 with it. In a murine (rat) cadaver model, the signal's spiral radius increased monotonically with glucose concentration despite pulsatile flow ($R^2$ = 0.91), and this monotonic behavior persisted through up to 6 mm of tissue. Although sensitivity decreased at higher glucose levels, each discrete concentration step remained clearly detectable. These results demonstrate that a shallow, passive implant paired with a commercial radar can effectively track blood glucose without requiring onboard electronics or batteries.

candidates.title: Uncertainty evaluation of length measurement by spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing
candidates.abstract: In this study, we evaluate the measurement uncertainty of spectral domain interferometry with super-Gaussian windowing, which has significant potential for interferometer-based dimensional calibration services owing to its simple configuration and nanometer-level precision. A super-luminescent diode (SLD) with a broadband spectrum was used as the light source for high-precision length measurement, and a frequency-calibrated spectrometer captured the spectral interference signal. The length measurement results were compared with a laser displacement interferometer. To evaluate the measurement uncertainty, numerical simulations were performed by considering the intensity-noise level of the CCD in the spectrometer and the frequency-axis uncertainty of the spectrometer. Through a comprehensive uncertainty analysis supported by numerical simulations, the combined standard uncertainty of the measured length was evaluated as sqrt((10 nm)^2 + (9.7x10^(-6)xL)^2). The resulting uncertainty budget provides a metrological basis for extending SLD-based SDI with super-Gaussian windowing toward interferometric dimensional calibration tasks over the millimeter-scale range.

candidates.title: Active turbulent flows of dense persistent particles driven at constant velocity
candidates.abstract: We study dense assemblies of self-propelled particles with infinitely persistent active forces, driven at a constant average velocity $V$ along their propulsion directions. Because the velocity $V$ introduces a finite timescale, it plays a role analogous to the shear rate in globally-deformed amorphous solids, and the system approaches a transition analogous to a yielding transition as $V \to 0$. We construct a force-velocity flow curve which is of the Herschel-Bulkley type, with a finite force threshold for flow. As $V$ decreases, the instantaneous velocity field becomes increasingly dominated by rare, localized plastic events, which produce fat tails in the velocity distribution and coexist with a slow, spatially correlated flow of streams and vortices. Many such events must accumulate throughout the system to fully relax its structure, so that the flow patterns reorganize after particles have been driven over a few particle diameters. The spatial extent of these correlated flows grows rapidly as $V$ decreases, and becomes only limited by the finite system size in our simulations. The kinetic energy spectrum displays a robust $k^{-1/2}$ regime also found in self-propelled particles at large but finite persistence times. Approaching the flow threshold thus leads to the same active turbulent state as increasing the persistence time in dense active matter, while displaying both analogies and differences with the yielding transition in sheared glassy materials.

candidates.title: Periodic Modulation of Linear Polarization Fraction in Repeating FRB 20240114A
candidates.abstract: Long-term polarization changes in repeating fast radio bursts (FRBs) can probe their emission geometry and propagation environment. We searched for periodic variation in the degree of linear polarization (DOL) of FRB~20240114A using the polarization catalog from the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope. The sample contains 6,099 bursts detected on 95 observing days over $\sim 488$ days. The daily mean DOL series was analyzed using phase distance correlation and Lomb--Scargle periodograms over trial periods of 10--240 days. The strongest peaks occur at $119.91^{+2.67}_{-2.04}$ and $122.31^{+2.63}_{-2.82}$ days, respectively. The quoted ranges correspond to the period intervals above the global $3σ$ thresholds. Global false-alarm probabilities were estimated from \(10^7\) random permutations of the daily values among the fixed observing dates, with the full period search repeated for each permutation. The resulting probabilities are \(9.98\times10^{-4}\) and \(8.95\times10^{-4}\), corresponding to equivalent Gaussian significances of \(3.09σ\) and \(3.12σ\), respectively. As a supplementary check, the same analysis using daily median DOL yielded similar peaks near 120 days. A descriptive sinusoidal fit to all 95 daily mean DOL measurements at a fixed period of 119.91 days has a semi-amplitude of 3.23\%. Possible explanations include precession-driven changes in viewing geometry and variations in propagation conditions within a binary system.

candidates.title: Squeezing Drives Southward Magnetic Field Enhancement During 10 May 2024 CME-CME Interaction
candidates.abstract: The southward magnetic field carried by coronal mass ejections (CMEs) is a key driver of space weather events, yet how interacting CMEs amplify this field remains debated. The 10 May 2024 event, which produced the strongest geomagnetic storm since 2003, offers an ideal testbed for this question. Combining multi-spacecraft observations with high-resolution controlled numerical experiments, we track the CMEs continuously from their origin near the solar surface to beyond Earth, and find that inherent squeezing during CME-CME interactions generates the sustained enhancement of the southward field, exceeding 60 nT in magnitude near Earth. First driven by the dynamic pressure of the trailing CME and later maintained by magnetic and thermal pressures at the CME-CME interface, squeezing transforms the preceding CME from a bulky cloud into a flattened "pancake" structure, prevents expansion-induced field decay, and maintains an amplified southward field over long distances. The strength of this enhancement scales with the intensity of the squeezing. Our findings establish a direct link between CME-CME interaction and strong southward fields, laying a physics-based foundation for understanding and forecasting the geoeffectiveness of interacting CMEs.
candidates.comment: Accepted for publication in ApJL. 15 pages, 7 figures

candidates.title: Phases of deformed sine dilaton gravity and JT limit
candidates.abstract: We study the implications of marginal deformation in sine dilaton gravity (sDG). We investigate the thermodynamic properties of deformed sine dilaton gravity (dsDG) and examine the phase stability of black holes in two space-time dimensions. We found that the deformation parameter ($λ$) sets a critical temperature threshold ($T_0$). Below this critical value ($T<T_0$), the system enters an unphysical phase characterized by a fractional density of states and a negative Wald entropy. Above the critical temperature ($T>T_0$), we obtain a physical black hole phase with positive entropy and negative free energy. Furthermore, we evaluate the Komar integral, derive the Casimir function for dsDG, and establish the first law of black hole thermodynamics. Finally, we explore the infrared (IR) limit of dsDG which we identify as Jackiw-Teitelboim (JT) gravity accompanied by marginal deformation. We also perform a detailed analysis of various thermodynamic entities pertinent to this deformed JT solution.

candidates.title: Local gluing classification and bulk-locked clock rings for $\mathbb{Z}_N$ models on a Klein bottle
candidates.abstract: We classify local reflection gluings of the $\mathbb{Z}_N$ plaquette model on lattice Klein bottles and solve the obstructed literal seam. Within the monomial far-corner ansatz, all commuting gluings form a family labelled by a unit $u$ of $\mathbb{Z}_N$. They exist for every $N$ at even seam length and, at odd length, exactly when $-1$ is a square modulo $N$. We determine the anyon transport, including exchange seams with $P^2=C$ for charge conjugation $C$, and the relation phases that distinguish an unfrustrated code from a commuting but frustrated Hamiltonian. For the literal gluing, the $2L_x$ noncommuting plaquettes form self-dual clock rings whose sectors are locked by the bulk. This gives an exact reduction of the spectrum to clock-ring spectra, closed-form ring ground energies for $N=2,4$, and a closed-form ground-state degeneracy. We further determine twisted-coefficient homology on the stated surface domains and compare it with logical modules on registered lattice grids; composite dimensions need not give squares of cyclic groups. Dressed-isometry gates and monodromy are reported with their finite-grid scope. Finally, the qudit Gottesman--Knill theorem bounds the computational interpretation: Clifford deformations and Weyl measurements with stabilizer inputs and no external magic states cannot supply a non-stabilizer resource. Charge-conjugation measurements that do supply such states lie outside this operation model. The new results concern explicit seam classification, phase-sensitive consistency and bulk-locked spectra, not a new general no-go theorem or a universal computing architecture.
candidates.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures; supporting code and data included as ancillary material

candidates.title: Reference-Assisted Qutrit Control and Conditional One-Round Distillation in a Charge-4e Superconductor Model
candidates.abstract: We formulate a charge-$4e$ parafermionic-vortex route to qutrit processing as a conditional theory with explicit operational assumptions. Sector preservation and same-label charge-conjugation covariance imply closure for every adaptive visible record. For charge-conjugation-invariant inputs, record probabilities are independent of the supported reference state; for arbitrary inputs, discarding the reference gives a population-weighted mixture of conjugate sector maps. We give a finite-depth stability bound for complete labelled instruments, including postselection and initial zero-sector contamination. A self-contained calculation reproduces the known dense single-qutrit closure of the registered Clifford-plus-Flip gate set. We also specify an abstract ternary CSS $[[11,1,5]]_3$ syndrome/recovery decoder: 243 classical representatives per CSS component correct all 3,609 Pauli errors of support weight at most two, and an exact integer dynamic program yields the full independent-Pauli logical enumerator.
